label: What are we treating? The need for broader provider understanding of POTS, its nature, and care.
summary: Postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome (POTS) as conventionally defined is a chronic condition (typically > 3 months duration) incorporating reproducible symptoms of orthostatic intolerance (including dizziness/lightheadedness, and near-syncope) in the absence of orthostatic hypotension (ie, absence of a sustained systolic blood pressure drop > 20mmHg with upright posture).
